headline: LongZero uses self-generated tasks to train long-context reasoning without an external corpus
summary: LongZero is a preprint method for generating long-context reinforcement-learning tasks without an external document corpus or larger teacher for its reasoning-task synthesis. A target model first writes questions, evidence and answers for fictional worlds, then expands those facts into long multi-document contexts; it also creates retrieval conversations, filters for questions it answers inconsistently, and trains with GRPO. On five benchmarks, the authors report mean-of-two-run average-score gains for Qwen3-4B-Thinking-2507 (54.68 to 57.42) and Qwen3-8B (44.63 to 45.66). The Qwen3-8B LongBench v2 score does not improve (32.01 versus 32.11 baseline), and 120/200 of its AA-LCR responses contain no answer. The results remain author-reported, limited to two Qwen checkpoints, short training and two runs; independent reproduction is open.
